title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration in Freshdesk
snippet:
The Freshworks Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI tools like Cursor and Claude to securely connect and interact with Freshdesk. The MCP server acts as middleware to expose specific capabilities, such as creating tickets, by using public APIs and supported authentication methods.

Note: Currently, Freshdesk allows you to authenticate requests involved in MCP integration by using an API key only.

```
This feature applies to the following products:
• Freshdesk Standalone 2021 (Latest version)
• Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026
```
Starting September 10, 2026, the Freshworks MCP integration is generally available. The rate limits and monthly action allowances for each plan are outlined below.
```
What counts as an MCP action?
An action is defined as a successful tool invocation via MCP. Examples of tool invocations. Examples:
• Fetch conversation related to the ticket with ID 1001 (1 action)
• Update the company name for the record with ID 11 to Apple (1 action)
```
| Supported plans | Rate limits (actions per minute) | Included MCP actions (per account, annually) |
|---|---|---|
| Growth | 25 | 1,200 |
| Pro | 50 | 6,000 |
| Enterprise | 100 | 12,000 |
```
Important:
• Pricing: To view current pricing and purchase add-on action packs, see Pricing.
• EAP transition:
• If you were on the Early Access Program (EAP), standard pricing and limits take effect on October 5, 2026.
• During the EAP, if you used the MCP integration on any plan other than Freshdesk Standalone 2021 (the latest version) or Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026 variant, the integration will stop working after September 10, 2026.
```
## **Supported MCP integrations**
Freshdesk supports MCP integration with any AI tool that provides MCP support. This section highlights a selection of commonly used integrations that you can connect to Freshdesk.

title: MCP Integration: Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
snippet:
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that enables AI assistants, such as Claude and Microsoft Copilot, to connect directly to Freshdesk. Through MCP, these assistants can perform actions on your behalf, such as creating tickets, updating contacts, or retrieving conversation history, without leaving the AI client.
Which Freshdesk products support MCP?
MCP is supported only in Freshdesk 2021 and Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026. Following is the compatibility matrix:
| **Product / Plan Variant** | **GA Support (Post-Sep 10, 2026)** | **Notes** |
|---|---|---|
| Freshdesk Standalone 2021 (Latest version) | Supported | Full support for GA release. |
| Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026 | Supported | Full support for GA release. |
| Legacy Freshdesk Variants (Pre-2021) / Other SKUs | Not Supported | EAP access ends September 10, 2026. |
Which AI clients are supported?
You can use any AI client that supports the MCP standard. Connect your preferred MCP-compatible client to Freshdesk using the MCP server URL and the API key provided in your Freshdesk administrator settings.
### Setup and configuration
How do I find my MCP settings in Freshdesk?
Go to Admin Settings > Apps & Integrations > MCP. On the MCP Details page, you can copy your MCP server URL, generate an API key, and manage your connection.

How does authentication work for MCP?
Freshdesk MCP uses API key authentication. Each user manually connects their AI client using their individual Freshdesk API key and the MCP server URL. You can find your API key in your Freshdesk profile settings.

Not yet. Freshdesk is not currently listed as a native connector in AI client marketplaces. To connect an AI client to Freshdesk via MCP, you must manually enter the MCP server URL and authenticate using your API key.

title: Introduction
snippet:
**Freshdesk MCP** is a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server that connects a [Freshdesk](https://www.freshdesk.com/) account to any MCP-compatible AI model or client. It exposes the Freshdesk API as a set of **tools** and **prompts** that can be invoked in natural language: the assistant can thus read and manage tickets, conversations, contacts, companies, knowledge base and custom fields.
The server is written in Python (FastMCP) with modular architecture (`core` / `services` / `schemas` / `tools`) and a shared HTTP client with rate limit management.
## What is it for¶
Once the server is connected, you can ask the assistant things like:
- "Show me ticket #12345 and its entire conversation"
- "Search for open and urgent tickets and assign them to the Support group"
- "Find the Acme company and create a contact for [mario.rossi@acme.it](mailto:mario.rossi@acme.it)"
- "Add a private note to ticket #12345 with analysis results"
- "Create a knowledge base article about resetting your password"
The model automatically chooses the correct tool and composes its parameters.
## Feature overview¶
- **124 tools exposed by MCP server**: 64 canonical `freshdesk_*` names and 60 legacy aliases deprecated. The aliases are associated with 59 handlers; `freshdesk_search_companies` exposes two of them.
- **2 guided prompts** (`create_ticket`, `create_reply`) to assist the model in composing payloads.
- **ToolAnnotations** on each tool (read / write / update / delete): behavior hints for safer automations.
- **Multi-tenant via HTTP**: a single deployment can serve multiple Freshdesk accounts, with credentials provided per-request.
- **Authentication via header** (`X-Freshdesk-Domain` / `X-Freshdesk-Api-Key`) preferred to query string.
- **Read-only** mode on tickets via `FRESHDESK_TICKETS_READ_ONLY`.
- **Context-safe attachments**: metadata is returned by default, base64 content only on request (1 MiB per file and 5 MiB overall by default).
- **Automatic pagination** of the conversation thread, up to 50 pages of 100 messages.

title: GitHub - romain-devsquare/fresh-desk-mcp
snippet:
# Freshdesk MCP Server
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for interacting with the Freshdesk API over HTTP (Streamable HTTP transport). Provides tools to manage tickets, contacts, agents, and more.
## Setup
```
npm install
npm run build
npm start
```
## Environment Variables
| Variable | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `FRESHDESK_DOMAIN` | Your Freshdesk domain (full hostname) | `yourcompany.freshdesk.com` or `support.yourdomain.com` |
| `PORT` | HTTP port (default `3000`) | `3000` |
## Authentication
The Freshdesk API key is passed via the `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>` header on the MCP connection. It is captured on session initialization and used for all subsequent Freshdesk API calls in that session.
## Docker
```
docker build -t freshdesk-mcp .
docker run -d -p 3000:3000 -e FRESHDESK_DOMAIN=yourcompany.freshdesk.com freshdesk-mcp
```
The MCP endpoint is available at `http://your-host:3000/mcp`.
## Claude Configuration
### CLI
```
claude mcp add --header "Authorization: Bearer <freshdesk-api-key>" --transport http freshdesk https://your-domain.com/mcp
```
### Manual (settings JSON)
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"freshdesk": {
"type": "url",
"url": "https://your-domain.com/mcp",
"headers": {
"Authorization": "Bearer <freshdesk-api-key>"
}
}
}
}
```
## Available Tools
| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `list_tickets` | List tickets with pagination and filters |
| `get_ticket` | Get a single ticket by ID (with optional includes) |
| `search_tickets` | Search tickets using Freshdesk query language |
| `get_ticket_conversations` | Get replies and notes for a ticket |
| `add_note_to_ticket` | Add a private or public note to a ticket |
| `reply_to_ticket` | Send a reply to a ticket |
| `create_ticket` | Create a new ticket |
| `update_ticket` | Update ticket properties |
| `delete_ticket` | Delete a ticket |
| `list_contacts` | List contacts (filterable by email/phone) |
| `get_contact` | Get a contact by ID |
| `list_agents` | List support agents |
| `get_agent` | Get an agent by ID |
| `list_groups` | List groups |
| `get_ticket_satisfaction_ratings` | Get satisfaction ratings for a ticket |
| `get_ticket_time_entries` | Get time entries for a ticket |

title: Hermes Agent for Freshdesk: how to connect it safely (2026)
snippet:
Hermes Agent for Freshdesk got much easier on September 10, 2026, when Freshdesk's own MCP server went generally available on Growth, Pro and Enterprise. Hermes can now talk to your tickets with one `url` and one API key in `config.yaml`, no community code required.
The catch is what that server hands over. Every API key gets all 37 tools, including `replyTicket`, and Freshdesk has no tool-level permissions. So the safety work moves into Hermes: list four read tools plus `createTicketNote`, give the bot its own agent seat, and keep it writing private notes. A sent Freshdesk reply can't be edited.
Budget for the metering too. Every MCP call is one action, reads included, and Growth includes 1,200 actions a year, which is roughly 240 drafted tickets before you pay $15 per 1,000. If what you want is AI actually working your Freshdesk queue, [eesel](https://www.eesel.ai/integrations/freshdesk) connects with the same API key, rehearses on your past tickets before go-live, and doesn't bill by the tool call.

Up until recently, if you wanted an outside agent on Freshdesk, it was community code or a wrapper you wrote yourself around the [Freshdesk API v2](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/freshdesk-api-v2). Now Freshdesk runs a server of its own. Per its [MCP article](https://support.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/articles/50000012670-model-context-protocol-mcp-integration-in-freshdesk-eap-), "Starting September 10, 2026, the Freshworks MCP integration is generally available."
The headline facts, which all come from Freshdesk's [MCP FAQs](https://support.freshdesk.com/en/support/solutions/articles/50000014407) and that same article:
- **Plans:** Growth, Pro and Enterprise, on the 2021 Standalone or Omni 2026 versions only. Legacy accounts aren't supported.
- **Endpoint:** `https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp`. Custom domains don't work.
- **Auth:** API key only, and calls follow that user's role permissions.
- **Tools:** 37, covering tickets, conversations, contacts, agents, groups, companies and help center articles. No delete or merge tools.
- **On by default.** An admin can switch it off under Admin Settings > Apps & Integrations > MCP.

| Route | How Hermes uses it | Holds your credentials | Reviewed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Freshdesk's official MCP server | Remote `url` under `mcp_servers` | Your Freshdesk API key, in a header | Freshworks |
| [effytech/freshdesk_mcp](https://github.com/effytech/freshdesk_mcp) | Local `uvx freshdesk-mcp` process | API key in env v

title: Freshdesk MCP Server — Easy Connect
snippet:
# Freshdesk MCP Server
Connect to the Freshdesk MCP server to manage tickets, reply to customers, update contacts and companies, and author knowledge base articles using AI agents on Gumloop, Claude, or Cursor.
## MCP server URL
```
https://mcp.gumloop.com/freshdesk/mcp
```
## Works with
## Tools 98
- List Tickets
List Freshdesk tickets with optional filters.
- Get Ticket
Get a Freshdesk ticket by ID.
- Create Ticket
Create a Freshdesk ticket. Requires `email` or `requester_id` to identify the requester.
- Update Ticket
Update fields on a Freshdesk ticket.
- Delete Ticket
Soft-delete a Freshdesk ticket. Restore via the trash within 30 days.
- Search Tickets
Search Freshdesk tickets using the filter DSL.
- Merge Tickets
Merge secondary Freshdesk tickets into a primary ticket.
- Forward Ticket
Forward a Freshdesk ticket as a new outbound email.
- Restore Ticket
Restore a previously soft-deleted Freshdesk ticket.
- List Conversations
List replies and notes on a Freshdesk ticket.
- Reply To Ticket
Post a public reply to a Freshdesk ticket.
- Add Note
Add a note (private by default) to a Freshdesk ticket.

The Freshdesk MCP server gives AI agents access to your Freshdesk helpdesk. That means agents can search and read tickets, post public replies and private notes, move tickets through their lifecycle, merge and forward duplicates, update contacts and companies, draft and publish knowledge base articles, manage community forum topics, and log time entries. It works across the full Freshdesk support stack, from a single ticket to your contact and company CRM, the knowledge base, and the community forums.

MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. It is an open standard that gives AI agents a way to connect to external tools and services. Instead of writing code against the Freshdesk API, encoding your API key for HTTP Basic auth, and parsing JSON responses yourself, you add your Freshdesk subdomain and API key to Gumloop once. After that, you can run your support desk just by chatting with your AI agent.
## What you can do with Freshdesk MCP on Gumloop
- ### Manage the full ticket lifecycle
Create, update, and triage tickets with full field control over status, priority, group, responder, tags, SLA dates, and custom fields. Merge duplicate tickets into a primary, forward a ticket as an outbound email, and soft-delete or restore tickets when plans change.
- ### Search tickets, contacts, and companies with the filter DSL
Run structured queries with Freshdesk’s filter
